zh_summary: @KobeissiLetter: US equity ETFs drew a record +$1.4 trillion over 12 months, tech funds +$65 billion (over double cyclicals) and defensives +$25 billion, versus +$850 billion the prior 12 months.
en_summary: @KobeissiLetter: US equity ETFs drew a record +$1.4 trillion over 12 months, tech funds +$65 billion (over double cyclicals) and defensives +$25 billion, versus +$850 billion the prior 12 months.
text:
BREAKING: US equity ETFs have attracted +$1.4 trillion in inflows over the last 12 months, their largest 12-month inflow on record.

Tech funds alone have attracted +$65 billion, more than double the inflows into cyclical equity ETFs.

At the same time, defensive equity ETFs have drawn +$25 billion.

In the preceding 12-month period, US equity ETFs attracted +$850 billion.

By comparison, during years 1 and 2 of the current bull market, inflows totaled +$300 billion and +$650 billion, respectively.

Investors are piling into US equity funds at a record pace.

name: Satya Nadella
zh_summary: @satyanadella: new Microsoft research in @Nature shows machine learning can improve weather forecasts two to six weeks out, aiding extreme weather prep, resources and agriculture. $MSFT
en_summary: @satyanadella: new Microsoft research in @Nature shows machine learning can improve weather forecasts two to six weeks out, aiding extreme weather prep, resources and agriculture. $MSFT
text:
In @Nature this week, our new research shows how machine learning can improve weather forecasts two to six weeks out, a timeframe that's historically been very difficult to predict.

It's exciting to see the potential of this work to help us better prepare for extreme weather, manage natural resources, and make more informed decisions in agriculture.

There's a broader lesson here... the future may not just be about ever-more-capable models, but about building intelligent verification systems around them: systems that learn where models are systematically wrong, reason about cause and effect, and continuously calibrate predictions against reality.

Read more: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/story/new-ai-framework-bridges-a-critical-gap-in-mid-range-weather-forecasts/

In @Nature this week, our new research shows how machine learning can improve weather forecasts two to six weeks out, a timeframe that's historically been very difficult to predict.

There's a broader lesson here... the future may not just be about ever-more-capable models, but about building intelligent verification systems around them: systems that learn where models are systematically wrong, reason about cause and effect, and continuously calibrate predictions against reality.

Read more: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/story/new-ai-framework-bridges-a-critical-gap-in-mid-range-weather-forecasts/

This marks the fourth-straight year with the US fiscal deficit around $2 trillion.

The deficit spending crisis is out of control.

name: Luke Gromen

en_summary: @LukeGromen: US interest plus entitlements is 105% of receipts in a good economy and growing 2.5x faster; doing nothing, cutting entitlements or cutting defense all lead to USD up and rates up until the system crashes or the Fed prints.
text:
because you're not identifying the problems, IMO.

US Interest + Entitlements is 105% of receipts in a good economy, growing 2.5x receipts.  Do nothing, you're going to get USD up, rates up, until system crashes or you print.

Cut Entitlements, you get USD up, receipts down, deficit up, rates up, until the system crashes or you print.

Cut defense, you get USD up, rates up, deficit up, until the system crashes or you print.

The only option they have is cut rates toward 0% and shift issuance forward.  My gold proposal is one way of doing that.

That's the only way out now.
